newsitem.title: USA: Ill. judge allows Tollway bond trustee into suit.
newsitem.headline: Ill. judge allows Tollway bond trustee into suit.

text.p: An Illinois judge on Tuesday allowed the trustee for $979 million of Illinois State Toll Highway Authority bonds to intervene in a lawsuit challenging its budget practices that has raised credit concerns among the rating agencies.

First National Bank of Chicago, a unit of First Chicago NBD Corp, serves as trustee over all Toll Authority debt and had contended that the agency could not adequately represent the interests of bondholders.
"I just don't see any reason to keep them out," Cook County Judge Stephen Schiller said.
Schiller had earlier ruled that the Toll Authority's practice of appropriating funds without oversight of the governor or General Assembly did not meet state constitutional requirements.

Schiller also entered an order enjoining the Toll Authority from any expenditures except debt service effective December 15, leading Moody's Investor's Service, Standard & Poor's and Fitch Investors Service to raise credit concerns over the bondholdings.
Toll Authority lawyers have said they will appeal Schiller's ruling to the Illinois Supreme Court. They have until July 11 to proceed with their appeal.

The leaders of three large debt issuing state agencies which do not need a state appropriation or receive state approval for their budgets have also said they are closely following the progress of the Tollway lawsuit.
Illinois Development Finance Authority has about $5 billion outstanding debt, Illinois Housing Development Authority $2 billion and Illinois Educational Facilities Authority $1.35 billion.
Lawyers Lee Schwartz and Myron Cherry representing the toll payers also asked Tuesday for the court to certify the lawsuit as a class action.

They also have sought to amend their complaint to include counts making the Toll Authority commissioners liable for any misappropriation of funds and to put the agency's vendors on notice that they might not get paid and may be required to return money improperly appropriated to them.
Those requests will be briefed by the attorneys, who are not scheduled to return to Schiller's courtroom until August 6.
